name: Wyoming
overview: In Wyoming, each county treasurer sells delinquent real property taxes at a tax sale; the buyer gets a certificate of purchase (a tax lien), not the property. State law lets these sales be made by lottery or by public auction to the highest bidder for cash, and the lottery-style draw is what the large counties describe. The treasurer signs and delivers a certificate of purchase to each buyer, and certificates can be assigned to someone else by endorsement. Redemption terms, interest and the waiting period before a tax deed are summarized on each county's own page below.

counties.how_to_bid: Register in person on sale day (7:45 am); the name on the registration must match the name on the payment, and each taxpayer ID gets one buyer number. Buyer numbers are drawn at random; when yours is called you may buy one property by calling its property number, or pass. Leaving the room forfeits your number. Pay in full by 5 pm on sale day. The owner may redeem in the 4 to 6 years after the sale.

counties.how_to_bid: Pre-register in person at the Treasurer's office and get an assigned number; you need it to enter the sale. Numbers are drawn at random by computer software, and the person whose number is drawn may complete the purchase of the tax lien for the parcel. The name on the pre-registration form must match the name on the payment; no realty, company or corporate names on checks or cards. The buyer receives a certificate of purchase, not title. Property that does not sell is bid in for the County. Redemption and other rules are in Wyoming Statutes §39-13-108(e).

counties.how_to_bid: Register on sale morning from 8:00 to 9:00 AM at the Uinta County Complex, 225 9th St. (new participants bring a W9 and a registration form); you must be present and over 18. It is a lottery: bidder numbers are drawn electronically, an equal number of times, and the person drawn may pay the advertised amount (delinquent tax, advertising fees and a CP fee) for a Certificate of Purchase, or decline. Check or cash only. The owner may redeem within four years by paying the amount paid at the sale plus 3% and 15% interest per year. The brochure says a CP holder may apply for a tax deed if the account stays unpaid over 5 years and loses that right six years after the sale; the tax deed fee is $25.00 plus recording fees. Reassignment costs $20.00 and is not allowed in the first 30 days.
